subject: Reconciling deployment constraints & dedicated sizing — BrioRetail follow-up
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Park <simon.park@brioretail.com>, Anita Gomez <anita.gomez@brioretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Reconciling deployment constraints & dedicated sizing — BrioRetail follow-up

Hi Simon / Anita —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can land a recommended Dedicated configuration for BrioRetail. You were very clear that latency and price-per-call both matter, and that you need the solution to run behind your VPC later this year. Below are the items we discussed and what we need to finalize sizing.

1) Expected steady TPS (inference requests per second): you called out 60 steady-state TPS with 300 TPS short bursts during promo spikes — is that still right?
2) Average token mix (client -> model -> response): you said average prompt length ~120 tokens and average generated length ~420 tokens, with ~15% of requests returning long-form summaries (~1,000 tokens). Confirm?
3) Model family + quality target: you indicated preference for a 13B-70B family model (semantic accuracy > 92% on internal evals). We should decide between H100-optimized 70B vs A100 80GB quantized 30B variant.
4) SLAs & region: required 99.9% monthly uptime and primary region us-west. Also asked about private deployment timing for Q1 2027.

What we need from you (action items):
- A 24–48 hour sample of production trace (anonymized) or a representative prompt set so we can run token distribution analysis.
- Confirmation on burst window tolerance (how long can you tolerate degraded tail latency during burst?).

Next steps on our side:
- We’ll prepare two recommended SKUs for Dedicated: a lower-latency H100 pool (single-model 70B) and a cost-optimized A100/quantized 30B pool with aggressive prefix caching.
- Planned deliverable: a short cost/latency comparison + suggested autoscale policy by end of day Friday (attached: brio-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx).

If you confirm the TPS and token assumptions above I’ll kick off the perf analysis with Aditya and Marissa.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications: 

- TPS: 60 steady is correct. Bursts hit 250–320 TPS but typically last 3–6 minutes (marketing-driven spikes). Short spikes (under 45s) are fine to be best-effort.
- Token mix: correct on avg prompt 120 / avg response 420. Long-form summary bucket is closer to 10% (my mistake on the call).
- Model: Prefer a balance — aim for the quantized 30B for baseline (cost-sensitive), but we want a 70B H100 fallback for high-fidelity during checkout flows. Can you support a multi-tier routing policy?
- SLA: 99.9% is the ask. Private deployment target is late Q1 2027 — earlier if we can meet compliance requirements.

I’ll get you a 48-hour anonymized trace by Thursday EOD. Also flagging that procurement wants capacity and commitment options: they asked for estimated committed monthly vCPU/GPU hours and a ballpark discount for a 12-month reserved pool.

Simon
VP Product, BrioRetail
simon.park@brioretail.com

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding Simon's clarifications. Key updates: bursts 250-320 TPS for 3–6 minutes (short), long-form only ~10%, wants multi-tier routing (quantized 30B baseline, 70B H100 fallback), and procurement will ask for committed-hours/discounts. Simon will provide 48-hour traces by Thu EOD.

Proposed plan:
- Aditya: run the token-distribution analysis on the trace when it arrives; produce an estimated tokens/sec profile and 95/99p tail latency projections for A100-quant (30B) and H100 (70B) baselines.
- Marissa: draft two Dedicated SKU options (Committed 12-mo, and On-demand burst) with rough monthly costs and recommended autoscale thresholds (burst buffer sizing). Include suggested routing policy for checkout flows to hit higher fidelity.
- Jasmine (me): assemble an RACI and a short playbook for the private deployment gating items (KMS, VPC peering, audit logs).

Quick questions for sizing decisions:
1) For the baseline 30B quantized pool, do we assume 1 request per GPU can hold 2 concurrent contexts for 420-token avg output (i.e., concurrency=2)? Or do you want us to simulate concurrency=3 for headroom?
2) Do we treat long-form (1k tokens) as a separate class for autoscale (e.g., spin up temporary H100 workers) or route long-form to the baseline and accept longer WRT?

I’ll draft the two SKU options and share by Friday. Any preferences on preferred GPU families to model first? H100 for high-performance, A100-80GB for quantized 30B is the typical pair.

— Jasmine

Jasmine / Aditya — quick internal note after reviewing Simon's numbers and our capacity model:

- Recommendation (short):
  * Baseline Dedicated pool: 8 x A100-80GB nodes, each configured to host quantized 30B with concurrency=3. That maps to ~75 steady TPS headroom across the pool for avg token mix (120/420). Autoscale floor 6 nodes, max 14 nodes for burst padding.
  * High-fidelity fallback: 2 x H100-80GB reserved for checkout-critical routes (route by path header). These should be in the same AZ for tail latency. H100 nodes spun up for 70B single-concurrency runs; these handle the 10–20% of traffic we mark as checkout/high-fidelity.

- Rationale: quantized 30B at concurrency=3 on A100 gives strong cost-per-token while concurrency keeps GPU utilization high. We picked 8 nodes baseline because bursts (320 TPS) will be handled via autoscale + short H100 spillover; with the autoscale window tuned to 60s we can avoid overspending for 3–6 minute promos.

- Cost notes: 12-month committed pool pricing reduces monthly spend ~18% vs on-demand in our model. Include a separate line-item for VPC private deployment setup (one-time engineering integration & KMS onboarding).

- Ask for trace: Aditya — run two sims (concurrency=2 and concurrency=3) against the trace when Simon sends it and validate 95/99p tail latency. Also produce token-rate graphs so we can justify node counts.

I’ll author a short doc with the cost table and routing policy text (will attach redwood-dedicated-pricing-2026Q4.pdf). Jasmine — once we have the trace we can give Simon concrete committed-hours and a draft discounts table for procurement.

— Marissa
